findings.detail: A sparse checkout intentionally leaves tracked paths absent while retaining their skip-worktree entries in the index. The normalized collector preserves those entries, but the raw collector enumerates them and requires every regular-file operand to exist. A checkout containing src/ but excluding a tracked docs/file therefore aborts with 'raw working-tree file changed type or disappeared: docs/file', preventing either review workflow from collecting scope. Distinguish intentionally absent skip-worktree entries from files that disappeared during collection.
findings.evidence: working_tree_digest copies the index and runs git add without --sparse. raw_tree_digest then uses ls-files --stage without filtering skip-worktree entries and fails at the existence check. The installed git-sparse-checkout manual explicitly states that an absent skip-worktree file has its absence ignored; git-add documents that entries outside the sparse cone are not updated normally. Both canonical review-scope copies contain this path.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: intentionally absent sparse-checkout files abort raw collection

findings.detail: The limitations list still says that line-ending changes and edits removed by clean filters cannot be detected. That directly contradicts the new raw-tree comparison and the preceding paragraph. Remove this obsolete limitation so readers receive a consistent account of the new guarantee.
findings.evidence: invocation.md:86 says such edits are invisible because the digest uses stored content rather than disk bytes. review-scope now hashes raw_tree into snapshot, and codex-aspects:1203-1207 compares raw trees. scope-and-snapshot.md:45 and the new EOL and clean-filter tests describe these edits as detectable.
findings.title: Docs drift: the limitations list still excludes normalized-away edits

findings.detail: The generic loop instructions now prescribe only raw-tree comparisons when both captures have raw_tree, whereas the implemented contract unions normalized and raw comparisons. If a clean filter's output changes while its input bytes stay fixed, following these instructions omits the affected file from the ledger even though codex-aspects changes reports it. Prescribe the same union recursively in both workflows.
findings.evidence: reviewers.md:137 specifies a raw-only diff-tree command. codex-aspects:1196-1207 always compares normalized trees and additionally compares raw trees. scope-and-snapshot.md:53 explicitly documents that union. invocation.md:80 also describes only raw comparisons and should be aligned.
findings.title: Parallel paths: generic edit measurement omits normalized-tree changes

findings.detail: The simplification reporting step still obtains content diffs from before_tree and after_tree, which remain normalized identifiers. After a raw-only edit such as LF-to-CRLF conversion, changes now lists the file but this prescribed diff is empty. Specify raw-tree diffs for raw edits, including corresponding child trees, while retaining normalized comparisons where needed.
findings.evidence: codex-aspects:1267-1290 populates before_tree and after_tree from .tree. SKILL.md:159 instructs reporting content with review_diff <before_tree> <after_tree>. The new EOL regression deliberately keeps .tree equal while changes reports f.txt, so that command cannot display the measured edit.
findings.title: Parallel paths: simplification content reporting still uses normalized trees

findings.detail: The legacy-format test removes raw_tree from two captures whose normalized trees are already equal, then expects an empty changed list. It therefore passes if legacy comparison is replaced with an unconditional empty result. Add a normalized content difference and assert its changed and outside_scope paths; also cover a mixed old/new pair.
findings.evidence: The clean-filter case at lines 71-74 establishes equal .tree values for the before/after captures. Lines 110-114 reuse those captures, delete raw_tree, and assert only []. Skipping comparison whenever either capture lacks raw_tree produces exactly the same expected output. Defect planting was not run.
findings.title: Tests that cannot fail: legacy coverage cannot detect a missing fallback comparison
